WITH film_actor_counts AS (
  SELECT f.film_id, COUNT(fa.actor_id) AS actor_count
  FROM film AS f
  LEFT JOIN film_actor AS fa ON fa.film_id = f.film_id
  GROUP BY f.film_id
), first_average AS (
  SELECT AVG(actor_count) AS avg_actor_count
  FROM film_actor_counts
), above_first AS (
  SELECT c.film_id, c.actor_count, c.actor_count - a.avg_actor_count AS excess_first
  FROM film_actor_counts AS c
  CROSS JOIN first_average AS a
  WHERE a.avg_actor_count IS NOT NULL
    AND c.actor_count > a.avg_actor_count
), second_average AS (
  SELECT AVG(actor_count) AS avg_actor_count
  FROM above_first
), above_second AS (
  SELECT c.actor_count, c.excess_first,
         c.actor_count - a.avg_actor_count AS excess_second
  FROM above_first AS c
  CROSS JOIN second_average AS a
  WHERE a.avg_actor_count IS NOT NULL
    AND c.actor_count > a.avg_actor_count
)
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(actor_count), 0) AS total_actor_count,
       AVG(excess_first) AS average_excess_over_first_average,
       AVG(excess_second) AS average_excess_over_second_average
FROM above_second;

assumptions.assumption: Every film is included in the first average; a film with no linked actors has a count of zero. If either stage has no non-NULL average, no films pass that stage, and the final total is zero while the two averages remain NULL.
